summary: This standards-track memo defines MIB objects for managing the line-code-specific parameters of VDSL interfaces that use single carrier modulation. Operators can monitor and configure those lines with SNMP.

plainLanguage.summary: Some fast internet lines over phone wires work in a particular way. This document defines the controls and readouts for managing lines that use this style.

subtitle: SNMP objects for configuring and monitoring the single-carrier radio side of VDSL phone-line broadband.

tldr.problem: The base VDSL MIB covers only line-code-independent settings, so lines using Single Carrier Modulation (SCM) had no standard way to manage their band-level parameters.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4069 defines the optional VDSL-LINE-EXT-SCM-MIB: one table of configuration profiles per band and one read-only table of the current physical state of each band, indexed alongside the VDSL-LINE-MIB.
tldr.outcome: An SCM VDSL agent does not need it to comply with RFC 3728, but if it is implemented the whole vdslSCMGroup MUST be implemented.

today: RFC 4069 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2005. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends the VDSL-LINE-MIB of RFC 3728.

sections.title: The Management Framework Context
sections.content:
RFC 4069 defines a MIB module, a set of managed objects that network management software reads and writes, normally through SNMP. The objects are written in SMIv2 (RFC 2578, RFC 2579 and RFC 2580), and the overall framework is described in RFC 3410.

The module is named VDSL-LINE-EXT-SCM-MIB and is an optional extension to the VDSL-LINE-MIB of RFC 3728, which handles the line-code-independent objects of Very High Speed Digital Subscriber Lines (VDSL).
sections.plainLanguage: Think of a big control panel for a machine. This document adds one extra panel for machines that use one particular kind of signal.

sections.title: What the Extension Covers
sections.content:
The module manages the line-code-dependent Physical Medium Dependent (PMD) layer of SCM VDSL lines. It is based on VDSL specifications from T1E1, ETSI and ITU, and takes the DSL Forum's management framework into account.

It sits under MIB-2 transmission. The module description says its objects MUST NOT be used for lines that use Multiple Carrier Modulation (MCM) line coding. If a line that does not use SCM refers to one of these objects, the object has no effect on that line.

The RFC also fixes short naming conventions: Vtuc is the VDSL transceiver at the near (central) end, Vtur the one at the remote end, Curr means current, Atn attenuation, Mgn margin and PSD power spectral density.
sections.plainLanguage: The new panel only works for lines that use this one signal style. If you plug a different kind of line into it, the dials do nothing.

sections.title: Tables and Objects
sections.content:
The single group, vdslSCMGroup, holds two tables. vdslLineSCMConfProfileBandTable holds transmit-band configuration, indexed by the profile name from the base MIB plus a band identifier. vdslLineSCMPhysBandTable is read-only and is indexed by ifIndex plus the band identifier. Each describes up to five bands, and unused bands are marked as unused.

The band identifier is a textual convention, VdslSCMBandId, with seven named values from the optional band through the first, second and third downstream and upstream bands.

Each configuration entry has an in-use flag, a center frequency in Hz, a symbol rate in baud, a constellation size (0..16, in log2 units), a transmit PSD level in units of -0.25 dBm/Hz and a RowStatus. The physical table has matching read-only Curr objects plus two measurements: the noise margin (CurrSnrMgn, in 0.25 dB) and the attenuation (CurrAtn, 0..255 in 0.25 dB).

A profile named DEFVAL always exists, with vendor-specific values unless the document says otherwise. A row cannot be changed while it is active, and a profile must be unreferenced from all lines before it is taken out of service or destroyed.
sections.plainLanguage: Each part of the signal gets its own row of settings, like a volume, a pitch and a strength knob. A second table is just a set of gauges that show what the line is really doing right now.

sections.title: Persistence
sections.content: All read-create objects in the module SHOULD be stored persistently, so settings survive a restart. The RFC gives an exhaustive list of these objects. It also notes that the interface indices used in this MIB are maintained persistently, and that View-based Access Control Model (VACM) data relating to them SHOULD be stored persistently as well (RFC 3415).
sections.plainLanguage: Settings should be written down in a notebook, not in chalk, so they are still there after the power goes off.

sections.title: Conformance and Compliance
sections.content: An SCM-based VDSL agent does not have to implement this MIB to comply with RFC 3728. If it does implement the extension, the group vdslSCMGroup is mandatory, and the module's compliance statement lists the 13 objects of vdslLineExtSCMGroup as mandatory. The existence of an entry in any of these tables is optional.
sections.plainLanguage: You do not have to build the extra panel. But if you build it, you must put all of its dials on it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The read-create objects in the configuration table may be sensitive. Unprotected SET operations can hurt network operations, and write access could let an end user raise their own service level or affect other users. A subscriber connected through the Vtur may also be able to manipulate the VDSL link and its embedded operations channel (EOC) for their own loop.

The readable physical-band objects are sensitive too, because knowing the bands in use could help someone apply deliberate interference. SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security, so implementers are RECOMMENDED to consider SNMPv3 with its cryptographic authentication and privacy, and deploying earlier versions is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.plainLanguage: Whoever can turn the knobs can make the line better or worse for everybody, so only the right people should be allowed to touch them.

sections.title: IANA Assignment
sections.content: IANA assigned the transmission value 228 to VDSL-LINE-EXT-SCM-MIB. That places the module's identity at { transmission 228 } in the MIB tree. The module's first and only revision is dated April 28, 2005.
sections.plainLanguage: The module got its own number in the big list of managed things, so nothing else will use the same one.
